ordered_diagnoses: Pulmonary Atresia with Intact Ventricular Septum

facts.raw_span: A 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf
progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency
temperature was 38.5 °C
heart rate, 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
respiratory rate, 60 breaths/min
jugular pulses were present and mucous membranes were cyanotic
a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
agitated saline contrast injected via the left jugular vein produced bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels
A 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf
progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency
temperature was 38.5 °C
heart rate, 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
respiratory rate, 60 breaths/min
jugular pulses were present and mucous membranes were cyanotic
a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects

concepts.why: The presence of a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice are consistent with Tricuspid Atresia.

The combination of cyanosis, jugular pulses, and a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, along with the presence of an interatrial defect and severe tricuspid regurgitation, are consistent with Tetralogy of Fallot.

The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, along with the presence of an interatrial defect and severe tricuspid regurgitation, are consistent with Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
The presence of severe tricuspid regurgitation, along with the presence of a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur and cyanosis, are consistent with Ebstein's Anomaly.
